statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-95690 ("Excessive Memory Allocation in DTLS Handshake Message Reassembly"): a DTLS client or server that receives crafted out-of-sequence handshake fragments allocates a buffer for the full declared message length for each buffered message, so a few small fragments can hold well over a megabyte per connection. Only DTLS endpoints reach this code, and the CVE record places it outside the FIPS module boundary. The CVE record lists OpenSSL 3.5.0 up to but not including 3.5.10 as affected (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-95690). The fix is proposed in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/33620 and, for the 3.5 branch, https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/33729 (both change ssl/statem/statem_dtls.c); neither is merged and no OpenSSL release carries it. Debian lists trixie as vulnerable, including 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-95690). Every published DHI Debian 13 openssl build (25 versions, amd64 and arm64, from the DHI Debian repository and the DHI security repository), including the FIPS builds, ships libcrypto and libssl from OpenSSL 3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9 (the version string in libcrypto.so.3) without a backport of this fix: the changelog shipped in libssl3t64 of every one of those builds has no entry for it, while the same check finds the entry for another backported OpenSSL fix (CVE-2026-35190) in the builds that carry it. Every build is affected.
